q: Enzymes are protein molecules formed in the living ____.
e: Enzymes are synthesized within cells as functional proteins.

q: They are biological catalysts and all the metabolic processes of the living things are catalysed by ____.
e: Enzymes accelerate biochemical reactions in organisms.

q: Enzymes that are isolated from the cell still retain their ability to ____.
e: Isolated enzymes remain active outside their native cells.

q: This property of enzymes is put to use in industrial processes which require high temperature or pressure to ____.
e: Enzymes enable milder industrial conditions than chemical catalysts.

q: They are much cheaper to use and the cost for industrial processes are reduced as they do not require expensive fuel to maintain high temperature to ____.
e: Enzymatic reactions lower energy costs in manufacturing.

q: Many enzymes used in industries are obtained from microorganisms mostly from fungi or ____.
e: Bacteria and fungi are common industrial enzyme sources.

q: Application of useful enzymes is seen in many industries like baking and brewing industries， dairy industry and textile ____.
e: Enzymes have diverse roles across multiple industrial sectors.

q: Even in medicine and pharmaceutical industry microbial trypsin is used to treat blood clotting and pancreatic trypsin is used for treatment of ____.
e: Trypsin has therapeutic applications in clot dissolution and anti-inflammatory treatment.

q: Commercial fermentation produces many enzymes that are useful to man. They include proteases， the protein-digesting enzymes and lipases， the fat-digesting ____.
e: Proteases and lipases break down proteins and fats respectively.

q: These enzymes are used to make biological washing powder and stains in clothes cause by blood， egg， gravy and grease can be removed ____.
e: Enzymatic detergents enhance stain removal efficiency.

q: The enzyme proteases act on red haemoglobin and break it down into smaller molecules which are colourless and dissolve in ____.
e: Degraded hemoglobin becomes water-soluble and washes away.

q: Both the protein and fat molecules are large but the proteases and lipases digest them into small， soluble substances which pass out of the fabric and are washed ____.
e: Solubilized stain components rinse out during washing.

q: Fungi produce the pectinases enzymes which are used in extracting fruit ____.
e: Pectinases facilitate juice release from fruit pulp.

q: The enzymes break down pectin， a jelly like substances between the cell walls and separate the fruit cells making it much easier for extracting the ____.
e: Pectin degradation disrupts cell adhesion, freeing juice.

q: During the break down process many kinds of polysaccharides (such as cellulose and starch) are also released causing the juice to become ____.
e: Polysaccharides increase turbidity in raw juice.

q: Pectinases continue to break them down to sugar making the juice sweeter and ____.
e: Further enzymatic action clarifies and sweetens the juice.
